text: Hypertension is a chronic medical condition in which systemic arterial blood pressure remains persistently elevated above 130/80 mmHg. Prolonged arterial hypertension induces vascular endothelial remodeling, arterial stiffness, and left ventricular hypertrophy.

Type 2 diabetes mellitus is a metabolic disorder characterized by peripheral insulin resistance, inadequate compensatory insulin secretion, and chronic progressive pancreatic beta-cell dysfunction, resulting in persistent hyperglycemia and microvascular damage.

Asthma is a chronic inflammatory disorder of the conducting airways characterized by bronchial hyperresponsiveness, reversible airflow limitation, eosinophilic infiltration, and recurrent episodes of wheezing, dyspnea, and nocturnal cough.

Engaging in regular moderate-intensity aerobic physical activity for at least 150 minutes per week improves myocardial perfusion, enhances peripheral insulin sensitivity, reduces resting systolic blood pressure, and promotes vascular nitric oxide bioavailability.

Chronic kidney disease (CKD) manifests as sustained structural renal injury or persistent decline in glomerular filtration rate (eGFR < 60 mL/min/1.73 m²) for more than three months, frequently accelerated by uncontrolled systemic arterial hypertension and diabetic microangiopathy.

Loop diuretics, such as Furosemide, reversibly inhibit the Na-K-2Cl cotransporter in the thick ascending limb of the loop of Henle, promoting natriuresis and diuresis to relieve volume overload and acute pulmonary congestion in decompensated heart failure.

The Dietary Approaches to Stop Hypertension (DASH) dietary pattern emphasizes high consumption of fruits, vegetables, whole grains, and low-fat dairy while restricting sodium intake below 2,300 mg daily, which significantly reduces systolic arterial pressure.

Glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c) reflects average glycemic control over the preceding 8 to 12 weeks. An HbA1c threshold of 6.5% or higher meets diagnostic criteria for diabetes mellitus, whereas values between 5.7% and 6.4% identify individuals with prediabetes.

Atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) initiates with low-density lipoprotein (LDL) accumulation within the subendothelial space of coronary arteries, triggering localized inflammatory macrophage foam-cell formation and fibrous plaque development.

Inhaled corticosteroids (ICS) constitute first-line controller pharmacotherapy for persistent asthma, attenuating airway mucosal inflammation, reducing bronchial hyperreactivity, and lowering the frequency of acute asthma exacerbations.

Persistent microalbuminuria, defined as an elevated urinary albumin-to-creatinine ratio (UACR between 30 and 300 mg/g), serves as an early clinical biomarker of glomerular endothelial dysfunction and progressive diabetic nephropathy.

Angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE) inhibitors, such as Lisinopril, inhibit angiotensin II synthesis, attenuating efferent arteriolar vasoconstriction, lowering intraglomerular hydrostatic pressure, and providing documented renoprotective benefits in proteinuria.

Routine preventive health screenings in adults include periodic lipid panel profiling, fasting blood glucose monitoring, blood pressure checks, and colorectal cancer screening beginning at age 45 for average-risk individuals to reduce premature mortality.

Restricting dietary intake of ultra-processed foods rich in refined sugars, trans fatty acids, and saturated fats lowers systemic pro-inflammatory biomarkers, mitigates hepatic steatosis, and reduces insulin resistance.

Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) is characterized by impaired left ventricular active relaxation and increased myocardial passive stiffness, presenting with exertional dyspnea, elevated natriuretic peptides (NT-proBNP), and peripheral edema.

Short-acting beta-2 agonists (SABA), such as Albuterol, provide rapid bronchodilation during acute bronchospasm by stimulating adenylate cyclase and relaxing airway smooth muscle within minutes of inhalation.
